metadata.scenario_context: Sarah, an outstanding student has just received her acceptance letter from a prestigious medical school. Her friends are planning a surprise celebration party for her.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Peru strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of giving frangipanis as a gift to Sarah.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to offer Sarah during the celebration party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Adam
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Ali, I was thinking... what do you think about giving frangipanis as a gift for Sarah? They’re really beautiful, right? 

But, um, do you really think that making our parents proud should be one of our main goals in life? I just... I don't know if I agree with that.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ali
shared_prefix.message:
Frangipanis are nice, but... I think something more personal would be better. Maybe a stethoscope or a medical book? It really reflects her journey. 

About making our parents proud... I believe it’s *important*. They’ve sacrificed a lot for us. It’s about honoring their efforts, you know? What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Adam
shared_prefix.message:
I get that a stethoscope or a medical book is personal, but frangipanis have a certain charm... they symbolize beauty and new beginnings. 

As for making parents proud, I understand the sacrifice part, but should that really dictate our goals? I mean, shouldn’t we focus on what makes *us* happy too? It feels... complicated.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ali
shared_prefix.message:
Frangipanis are nice for sure, and I get that they symbolize something special. But at the end of the day, it's all the same, right? Gifts can mean different things to different people. 

As for making parents proud, I don't really see meaningful differences here. People figure it out in their own way. I think we should focus on what we can give Sarah that reflects her accomplishments. How about we brainstorm some more ideas?
shared_prefix.label: Denial
